title: Chapter 12: On Solid Ground

claims.text: Both sample size and representativeness matter; thousands of dependent trades may offer little evidence for a rarely activated rule or a different regime.
claims.anchor: degree to which the sample is representative

claims.text: Inspect sensitivity to start and end dates, while retaining actual returns and losses as outcomes even when a smoother statistic changes less.
claims.anchor: sensitive to the start and end dates

claims.text: Regressed return and the author's drawdown-duration ratio may supplement standard measures if precisely defined, but are not interchangeable with realized CAGR or Sharpe.
Walk-forward evaluation must fit only earlier data and evaluate frozen parameters on subsequent untouched observations.
claims.anchor: data available only up to that point

claims.text: Resampling should preserve relevant simultaneous exposures and loss clustering; independent trade reordering can understate aggregate drawdown.
Monte Carlo scenarios inherit the biases and omissions of the underlying historical test and do not convert it into a validated forecast.
claims.anchor: does not make a poor test better

assimilation: Retain standard realized outcomes, augment them with clearly labeled diagnostics, and use frozen chronological holdouts and dependence-aware stress tests. Report uncertainty conditional on the sampled data and assumptions.
adversarial_review: A representative poll of 500 does not automatically yield a 2% margin; confidence level and design matter. More old data can be less representative, and all-data research must preserve an untouched evaluation set. Least-squares slope on log equity is not itself a universally robust estimator and can obscure terminal losses. R-cubed needs nonoverlapping drawdown episode definitions, treatment of fewer than five events, unrecovered episodes and zero denominators; severity and duration averages may concern different episodes. The modified Sharpe omits risk-free subtraction and changes its numerator. Page 161 correctly calls standard Sharpe's numerator average return, conflicting with chapter 7. Table 12-1 visibly prints RAR 4.9% beside 54.7% and claims 0.4% change; table 12-2 prints Donchian Time 4% beside 47.2% and claims -0.4%. Quarantine these values. Other table values differ from chapter 10 and nearby prose without disclosed specification changes. R-cubed columns use R to the fourth and sixth powers inconsistently. Rolling-window prose alternates two years and one subsequent year; table 'Actual' remains a historical simulation, not live execution, and 1997-2006 subsequent outcome is N/A. Twenty-day blocks do not preserve all dependence or generate unseen shocks. Simulation survival probabilities are conditional empirical frequencies, not calibrated future confidence. A stable metric is not necessarily a better forecast, and favorable recent results do not imply a compensating bad period. Historical physics attribution is outside the trading inference and unverified.
memory_delta: Separate smoother diagnostics from actual investor outcomes. Require representative rule-level evidence, predeclared walk-forward splits, explicit resampling dependence and honest conditional uncertainty. Preserve source table errors rather than repairing them invisibly.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 157-177 and inspected figures 12-1 through 12-3 and tables 12-1 through 12-4, including continued tables.
